title: Autonomous Line-Follower Robot
shortDescription: A responsive, two-wheel differential drive robotics platform engineered around the ATmega328P architecture with hardware-level PWM frequency calibration (TCCR0B 7.8 kHz) for high-precision path tracking.

detailSections.title: Overview
detailSections.content: Engineered and constructed in 2025, this autonomous robotics platform navigates complex tracks using high-speed differential drive kinematics powered by the ATmega328P microcontroller and an L298N dual H-bridge motor driver.
📷 Fig 1: Front chassis perspective showing the ATmega328P controller, battery pack, and differential drive platform.

detailSections.title: Hardware-Level PWM Frequency Calibration (TCCR0B Manipulation)
detailSections.content: Standard Arduino PWM switches at ~490 Hz or 980 Hz, causing audible motor whine and low-duty-cycle stalling under torque load. By directly configuring the TCCR0B timer/counter control register to set timer prescalers for ~7.8 kHz / 62.5 kHz operation, the motors deliver smooth, stall-free torque across micro-adjustments.
📷 Fig 2: Top chassis layout detailing the L298N dual H-bridge motor driver, power distribution switch, and motor leads.

detailSections.title: Sensor Array & Closed-Loop Control Algorithm
detailSections.content: The front bumper integrates high-sensitivity analog/digital IR optical sensors with threshold hysteresis. A tuned closed-loop proportional controller dynamically adjusts differential wheel velocities to negotiate sharp 90-degree corners, acute intersections, and speed straights.
📷 Fig 3: Optical IR line detection array mounted beneath the front bumper with threshold adjustment potentiometers.
